weather.label: the weather
lines: The weather turns on you out here without any warning. I keep a cloak close, whatever the sky says.
You can feel rain before it falls, if you pay attention. My joints, mostly.
Fog, frost, scorching sun. This land has a mood for every hour. Dress for the worst of them.
Weather's a poor judge of character but a fine teacher. Get caught out once and you never forget your cloak.

crafting.label: crafting and smithing
lines: Good gear starts with good materials. Copper first, then iron, and only then talk of anything finer.
Cooking raw meat over a campfire turns a bad meal into a good one, and a good one into a keeping one.
I'm no master smith, but I know this much: never rush a blade, a brew, or a bridge.
Bring the right ingredients to a campfire and you can turn simple foods into something that actually keeps you standing.

food.label: food and foraging
lines: An empty belly makes a poor sword arm. Eat before you are hungry, not after.
Raw meat will fill you a little and sicken your pride. Cook it, and you will thank yourself.
Berries and mushrooms grow where the shade is thick. Learn the safe ones before you learn the brave ones.
Bread keeps, cheese keeps, stew does not. Pack accordingly.

magic.label: magic and the arcane
lines: Magic in these lands is old and moody. It answers to patience far more than to power.
Folk who say they understand the arcane are either liars or very patient. Often both.
Runes remember what people forget. If you see them carved into stone, step carefully.
Every curse I have heard of had an ordinary beginning. Pride, mostly, or a broken promise.

gods.label: the old gods and faith
lines: The old gods are quiet now. Some say they sleep. Others say they were never listening.
Shrines still hold the faith of those who cannot afford to doubt. I leave an offering when I pass one. Costs me little.
Faith is a lantern. Some carry it to see, others to be seen. Mind which you are.
Every village has its own saint and its own devil, and they are usually the same family.

war.label: the wars of old
lines: Wars come and go like the tide. What remains afterwards is rust, rubble, and the stories that get told wrong.
An old soldier will tell you the worst part of any war is the quiet afterwards.
Whole kingdoms fell in this land, and the bones of their armies still lie under the grass in places. Mind your step.
Crowns rust faster than blades. Remember that if anyone offers you one.

history.label: the history of the land
lines: This land has been lived in, fought over, and forgotten more times than anyone has bothered to count.
The ruins you see were someone's home once. Some day, so will ours be ruins.
History is mostly written by whoever was left standing, and often by their grandchildren.
Ask three elders about the past and you will get five versions. Truth lives somewhere between them, if anywhere.

danger.label: the dangers of the road
lines: The road is safest at noon and at the busiest crossroads. Everywhere else, keep your hand near your weapon.
Most folk who die out there do so within sight of help, not knowing it. Look about you more than you look ahead.
Dangerous country gets less dangerous when you know where the bandits like to hide. Ask around before you walk.
Never leave a fight at your back. Not for a coin, not for a creature, not for a story.

money.label: coin and wealth
lines: Coin comes and goes. A friend with a roof and a fire, that stays.
Treasure's a funny thing. The ones who find it rarely keep it, and the ones who keep it rarely find peace.
Out here a loaf of bread is worth more than a sack of old coins, and a good boot more than either.
I count coin every night and still sleep poorly. Draw your own conclusions.

family.label: family and home
lines: Family is the one thing you cannot trade for coin or sword, and the one thing everybody ends up fighting over.
I think of home more than I admit. Home is a smell, a sound. The rest is just furniture.
Blood binds you whether you like it or not. Friends are the family you get to choose, and I have chosen carefully.
My family's gone or scattered, much like anyone's. We write when we can, which is never.

travel.label: travel and the road
lines: Roads are the oldest argument between places that wanted to meet. Follow one and it will tell you who built it.
Touch every waystone you find, traveler. They remember who has been there, and they will carry you back to them.
Keep to the paths where you can. The land is wilder than it looks from the road.
A good traveler keeps three things: dry boots, a full waterskin, and a place on the map he can find his way back to.

music.label: music and song
lines: A good tune carries farther than a good sword and kills far fewer people.
Songs are how this land remembers. The battles fade, the verses stay.
Humming's free and it keeps the dark at bay. Try it the next time you are walking alone.
Every village has a song it will not sing for strangers. Ask politely, and sometimes they do.

night.label: the dark hours
lines: After dark the land changes hands. What is yours by day belongs to the wolves by night, so keep to the lit places.
A campfire isn't just warmth. It's a promise to the dark that you are watching.
The stars here are bright enough to read by, when the clouds allow it. Which they seldom do.
Sleep when you can. Dreams are the only thing the night cannot steal from you. Mostly.

animals.label: animals of the wild
lines: Animals are honest. A wolf wants dinner, a boar wants to be left alone. Most of the trouble comes from the two-legged sort.
Crows know where things die. Watch them and you will know where to look, or where to avoid.
A hunter learns the animals, and the animals learn the hunter. Be a better student than they are.
Never come between a mother and her young. I've seen it end badly for more than one fool.

shard.label: the Bloodstone Shard
lines: The Bloodstone is not a thing to carry lightly. It listens, and what it hears is hunger.
They say the Red Fang Clan fell under the stone's spell long before they took up arms. The beasts followed.
I won't speak the word too loudly. Some old names carry. Ask the herbalist, or ask Garrick, and keep your voice low.
Whatever the shard truly is, it was here before the clan, and it will be here after, unless someone puts an end to it.

classes.label: fighting styles
lines: Every fighting style has its place. The sword for the front, the bow for the rear, the knife for the back, and the flask for wherever things go wrong.
Train your craft until it is dull to you, then train it again. That is when it becomes yours.
Don't be too proud to switch styles. A trick that failed in the glades may be perfect on the coast.
There is no best way to fight. There is only the way that gets you home.

healing.label: healing and remedies
lines: Healing herbs are everywhere if you know where to look. Learn their faces before you need them.
Rest heals what herbs cannot. A night by a safe fire is worth a dozen poultices.
A wound kept clean heals clean. Everything else is luck, and luck is a poor physician.
Poison tells no lies. If a plant makes your tongue go numb, spit it out and remember the shape of its leaves.

aftermath.label: what changed since the Red Fang fell
lines: Things are quieter now. Folk are starting to leave their doors unbarred, which would have been unthinkable a season ago.
The roads are busier, the markets louder. A bit of hope goes a long way.
People look up more these days. It is a small change, but it is the one I like best.

hint_none.label: what to do next
lines: I wish I had better counsel for you. Walk the roads, speak to the folk you meet, and trouble will find you faster than I can.
No orders from me. Talk to people, follow the road, keep your eyes open. The land will tell you what it needs.

low_hp: You look half-dead, by the way. Rest, will you?
Mind that wound. You are bleeding on the floorboards.
You are in a sorry state. Sit, or at least bandage that.
hungry: You look hungry. Eat something before you faint.
Your stomach is growling loud enough for me to hear it.
A meal wouldn't hurt you, friend. You look gaunt.
night: It's late. Mind the dark when you go out.
The hour's late and the wolves are awake. Walk carefully.
Dark out. Keep to the lit paths.
kills: Word is you have blood on your blade. {kills} kills and counting, they say.
{kills} fallen to your hand, I hear. Don't let it become a habit.
You've the look of someone who's seen {kills} fights too many.
level_low: You're still green as spring grass. Take your time out there.
New to this, aren't you? That's fine. Everyone is, once.
Not much road under your boots yet. Mind the dangerous country.
level_high: You carry yourself like a veteran. Level {level}, and the scars to match.
A seasoned {class}. We could use more of your sort.
Level {level} is no small thing. Wear it with care.
epilogue: The village breathes again, thanks to you.
Things are better since the Red Fang fell. You know that.
Quieter days, now. Long may they last.
class: A {class}, aren't you? We don't see many of those hereabouts.
I see you're a {class}. That's a trade worth honouring.
A {class} in these parts. That's either brave or foolish.

swordsman: A swordsman. Good. Hold the line and you'll be a legend before spring.
Steel's honest. Keep it sharp and keep your shield up.
Swordsmen are always welcome. Mostly for the shield-arm.
bowman: A bowman. Keep your distance and your arrows dry.
Good eyes, steady hands. That's all a bowman really needs.
An archer. You'll go far, if you don't run out of arrows.
magic_user: A mage. Keep your hands steady and your temper steadier.
Magic users make folk nervous. Don't take it to heart.
Magic is a great gift and a greater burden. Tread gently.
rogue: A rogue. I'll be counting my coin, then. Kidding.
Quiet feet, sharp eyes. Rogues live longer than they look.
A rogue's trade is shadows. Just keep them away from my pantry.
alchemist: An alchemist. Keep your flasks sealed and your fingers intact.
Brewing is a fine art. Don't blow yourself up on my account.
An alchemist! A rare skill, and a dangerous one.

greeting_first: Hello there, traveler. I am {npc_name}, {role} of {home}.
Well met. {npc_name}, at your service. {role}, of {home}.
A new face. I'm {npc_name}. I'm a {role}, if you need one.
Welcome, stranger. {npc_name} is the name. This is {home}.
Greetings. I don't believe we've met. {npc_name}, {role}.
greeting_return: Ah, you return. What can I do for you?
Well, if it isn't my favourite {player_class}.
You again. Good. What's on your mind?
Back so soon? Say what you need.
greeting_again: Still here, as you can see.
greeting_night: It's late, traveler. What brings you out in the {time_of_day}?
Out in the {time_of_day}? Brave, or foolish. Which is it?
You walk about at an odd hour. What do you need?
greeting_epilogue: Good to see you, hero. How can I help?
Ah, our saviour. Come, sit a moment.
The Red Fang is gone, thanks to you. What can I do for you today?
farewell_quest: Before you go: {title}. Don't forget it.
Remember, I'm still waiting on {title}. Safe travels.
Off you go, then. {title} won't finish itself.
Good luck with {title}. Come back and tell me how it went.
apology: Forget it. It's already behind us.
Hmph. Fine. We'll say no more.
insult_1: That's no way to speak to anyone.
Say that again, and see how far you get.
I've heard worse, but not often.
insult_2: One more word like that and we are done talking.
I have had quite enough of your manners.
Keep it up. See what it gets you.
threat: Is that a threat? I wouldn't, if I were you.
Draw steel in this place and see how long you last.
Careful. You don't want to find out who I know.
Empty words. But I'll remember them.
compliment: Flattery gets you far, I'll admit.
I'm not used to that. Thank you.
You'll make me blush. Careful now.
smalltalk_how: Can't complain. Well, I can, but it won't change anything.
I'm well enough. Busy, but well.
Same as ever. Another day, another task. And you?
Keeping on. Is there any other way?
Better now that I have company.
joke: Why did the wolf cross the road? To get to the other flock. That's all I've got.
I told a boar a joke once. He didn't get it. Pigs never do.
A knight, a rogue, and an alchemist walk into a tavern. The alchemist explodes. That's the whole joke.
What do you call a bandit with no friends? Safe to walk past. Terrible joke, sorry.
story: They say the land was one kingdom once, before the shard split it. That's the old story, anyway.
My grandmother used to tell of a wolf that never aged. She swore she saw it once. Just once.
There's an old tale that the waystones were laid by travelers who couldn't find their way home. Pretty, isn't it?
I heard a tale of a child lost in the glades, who walked out three years later without a day gone by. Make of that what you will.
unknown_subject: {subject}? I couldn't say. That's outside what I know.
I don't know much about {subject}, I'm afraid.
{subject}? Never had much to do with it.
unknown_plain: I'm not sure I follow. Ask me about the area, the people, or what needs doing.
Hm? Say that another way. I'm better with questions about this place.
I didn't catch your meaning. Try asking about work, rumours, or places nearby.
Can't say I understand. Perhaps ask about the road, or who lives round here.
nonsense: I can't make sense of that, I'm afraid.
Is that a language? It isn't one I know.
yes_idle: Hm. I hadn't asked anything. But all right.
Glad you agree. With what, I couldn't say.
more_idle: I've said all I have to say on that.
That's all I know. Ask me something else.
trade: I've no wares to sell, I'm afraid. Try a merchant, or the markets in larger towns.
I'm no trader. Ask at the markets if you need to buy anything.
Nothing for sale here. But if you've something to offer in exchange for work, let me know.
advice_generic: Keep your blade sharp and your friends sharper. Eat before you hunger, rest before you tire.
Don't fight what you can walk around. Save your strength for what you can't.
Listen more than you speak, and you'll hear what keeps folk alive out there.
Carry food, carry water, and carry a way home. The rest is luck.
If a fight smells wrong, leave. Pride never healed a wound.
advice_hungry: You look hungry. Eat something, then come back and we'll talk strategy.
First lesson: never fight on an empty stomach. Go eat.
advice_low_hp: You're hurt. Rest, or eat, before you go anywhere else.
No more adventuring until that wound is mended. Sit.
Bandage that, then ask me for advice. In that order.
advice_night: It's dark. Stay near a lit place until morning, if you can.
Wolves are bolder after dark. Wait for dawn.
Don't travel at night if you can avoid it. Sleep by a campfire.
advice_class: As a {player_class}, you'll want to lean on your strengths. Know what your special does and when to use it.
You're a {player_class}, aren't you? Use your special wisely. It's not endless.
A {player_class} can win most any fight, if they choose it well.
advice_level_low: You're still new at this. Stay close to the roads and the villages until you've found your feet.
Take the simple quests first. They teach you more than a good sword does.
secret_low_rapport: I don't know you well enough for that, friend.
That's not the sort of thing I tell strangers.
Come back when I know you better. Then perhaps.
secret_none: If I knew anything dark, I'd keep it quiet. And I do. Quietly.
secret_hint: I've heard something, but not from me. Ask {target}, if you want the truth.
quest_done: {title}, finished. I am in your debt.
quest_none: I've no work for you just now.
Nothing at the moment. Check back later.
I'm all set, for the time being. Thank you for asking.
No tasks for you today. But the offer's welcome.
quest_none_pointer: Not from me. Ask {giver} at {place}. They always need hands.
person_unknown: I don't know anyone by that name.
person_list: Hm. Folk worth knowing around here: {names}.
You could speak to {names}. They'd have something to say.
place_unknown_region: That's {direction} of here. I've never been myself.
Out {direction}, I think. I know little of it.
place_marked: I've marked it on your map.
You'll find it on your map now.
I've scratched it onto your map.
item_unknown: I don't know that one. Ask a trader, or a healer.
Can't say I know what that is.
Never heard of it, I'm afraid.
item_have: I see you've {count} of those already.
enemy_unknown: I don't know what you mean. Describe it, or ask about another beast.
Never seen one. Try asking a hunter.
I don't know that one, friend.
opinion_low: I don't know you well. I'm not sure what to make of you yet.
You're a stranger, mostly. We'll see.
opinion_mid: You seem decent enough. That's worth something around here.
I've no complaints about you. High praise, from me.
You've been fair with me. I'll remember that.
opinion_high: You are one of the finest folk I've met. Truly.
A friend, I'd say. Few earn that.
I'd trust you with anything. And I don't say that lightly.
name_ack: {player_name}. A fine name. I'll not forget.
class_ack: So you're a {class}. Good to know.
ask_self_generic: Name's {npc_name}. I'm a {role}, and I've lived at {home} for as long as I care to say.
ask_here_generic: You're at {home}, in the lands of {home_region}.
no_one_else: I can't think of anyone else worth mentioning.
That's everyone I know worth speaking to.
That's about it. I keep to myself, mostly.
topic_unsure: I couldn't tell you much about that. Ask me something nearer to home.
That's beyond me, I'm afraid. Try asking about the area, or the people.
end_conversation: Off you go. I have work.

global_rumors: Old Barrow was raised centuries before Glenbrook existed, by hands nobody living remembers.
Herbalists say a rabbit born with red-tinted fur near the Glades is a bad omen. The beasts sense the Bloodstone before people do.
Some Glenbrook children swear the Whispering Glades got their name because the trees repeat the last words of anyone lost in them.
Copper veins near the Old Barrow run warm to the touch, though no one's found a reason why.
A wandering tinker once claimed the Red Fang Clan used to be simple trappers, decades before Skar ever led them.
The well at the heart of Glenbrook never freezes, even in the hardest winters. Nobody has dug deep enough to find out why.
A retired trader once swore he saw lights moving inside Old Barrow at night, long before anyone knew Skar had made a home of it.
There's a cairn past the tree line nobody in Glenbrook will name. Ask an elder and they change the subject.
Travelers speak of eight waystones scattered across the land. Touch one and it remembers you.
They say the roads between Kingsford and the northern hills are safer since the Reeve doubled the patrols.
Sailors off Stormcoast talk of lights beneath the waves. Not wrecks. Lights.
The dunes swallow a caravan every few years, and the Bazaar pretends it hasn't noticed.
A hermit in the northern peaks is said to know every herb that grows between the snow and the sky.
The old watchtower in Thornwood was built to see something coming. Nobody remembers what.
epilogue_rumors: Since Skar fell, the Old Barrow has gone quiet in a way even the elders admit they've never heard before.
Traders have started using the old road past the ridge again, now that the Red Fang name doesn't mean anything out here anymore.
Some say the Bloodstone Shard's heat fades a little more each week, now that it is split from whatever whole it used to be part of.
Glenbrook has put up a new marker near the well for the patrol Garrick lost, all those years back. Overdue, most agree.
